**About Xanadu**
Xanadu’s mission is to build quantum computers that are useful and available to people everywhere.
  
  
At Xanadu, we are learners, innovators, researchers, collaborators and problem solvers. We are creating something that has never been built before. What we are doing is extremely hard, the classic moon shot. Few people in their life will be able to be a part of something like this, where if we are successful, the technologies we develop will solve some of the world’s most challenging problems, and literally change the world. And that is something to be excited about!
  
  
**Your Role And Responsibilities**
The successful candidate will join the cross-functional Data Analysis team to develop statistical models and measurement strategies that guide photonic component design. Working with photonics designers and experimentalists, you will distinguish measurement uncertainty from fabrication variability and translate experimental data into actionable design decisions.
  
  
The ideal candidate is an impact-driven data scientist capable of abstracting complex hardware problems, isolating leading-order effects from secondary issues, and translating those priorities into statistical models. Working closely with photonics designers and experimentalists, you will define the next generation of ultra-low-loss component designs and measurement procedures, directly impacting design optimizations at Xanadu's 200mm and 300mm fabrication partners.
  
  
**You Will**

- Develop statistical models to infer the characteristics of photonic devices from experimental datasets.
- Partner with photonics designers to develop measurement methods and test structures that distinguish competing explanations, reveal systematic errors, and improve parameter-estimation precision.
- Investigate reported uncertainties by finding and quantifying unknown systematics, building models to account for them, and devising methods to reduce errors.
- Build and maintain robust Python-based code to analyze measured data.

**Basic Qualifications And Experience**

- MSc or PhD in physics, statistics, applied mathematics, engineering, or a related quantitative discipline.
- At least two years of experience analyzing experimental or observational data to answer scientific or engineering questions (relevant graduate research counts toward this experience).
- Demonstrated ability to formulate statistical models connecting physical processes and measurement systems to observed data, identify dominant effects, and evaluate model assumptions.
- Strong applied knowledge of parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification, including identifying and modeling systematic effects, accounting for correlated errors, and propagating uncertainties into derived quantities.
- Experience solving inverse problems and assessing the reliability of inferred parameters through model diagnostics, sensitivity analysis, and validation against simulations or independent measurements.
- Experience designing or improving experiments, measurement procedures, or validation studies to distinguish competing explanations and reduce uncertainty.
- Proficiency in Python for scientific computing and data analysis, with experience developing reproducible, maintainable analysis code using version control, documentation, and appropriate tests.
- Ability to work with scientists and engineers across disciplines, translate open-ended hardware questions into tractable analyses, and communicate conclusions, limitations, and recommended next steps. Ability to prioritize work according to its expected impact on research and engineering decisions.

**Preferred Qualifications And Experience**

- Experience with hierarchical or multilevel models to distinguish sources of variation, such as measurement repeatability, device-to-device differences, and fabrication variability.
- Experience with Bayesian inference and computational methods such as Markov chain Monte Carlo, including assessing convergence and validating inference results.
- Experience with precision measurements, calibration, or metrology, including diagnosing systematic effects and using knowledge of the measurement apparatus to improve analysis.
- Familiarity with photonic integrated circuits, optical component characterization, semiconductor fabrication, or quantum optics.
- Experience turning research analyses into reusable software or automated workflows used by other scientists and engineers.

This is for a new position. Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and internal benchmarks. The base salary range is 100,000 - 140,000 CAD. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.
  
  
Our values are important. They are fundamental and lay the foundation for culture at Xanadu. Learn more about our values here.
  
  
We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We are committed to building an inclusive, safe, and equitable culture and fostering an environment where our employees feel included, valued, and heard. We are committed to meeting the needs of all individuals and support a barrier-free workplace. Should you require accommodations at any point during the recruitment process please contact Recruiting at recruiting@xanadu.ai.

The successful candidate will combine strong statistical and analytical judgment with the ability to build production-ready data products. ABOUT STOREFORCE 

StoreForce is deeply passionate about Retail – it’s in our roots and part of every single line of code we write. We’re known to say we’re Retailers first, and a technology vendor second. Every day we strive to help Retailers set a new standard for operational excellence,  changing the way retailers think, manage and perform.  
  
Now is a great time to be joining us as you can make a real impact in helping us accelerate our growth while working with some of the world’s best known retail brands. We thrive on change, collaboration, and trust and invest in, as well as support our people, celebrating diversity and fostering a space for them to learn and grow every day.  
  
From day one, you’ll get a warm welcome as well as the tools and information you need to perform at your best with regular one-to-ones and personal development planning for growth.  You’ll also have practical opportunities to learn from other experts and attend in person events to quickly feel integral to a growing and diverse global team.

OVERVIEW

Reporting to the VP, Technical Operations, the Senior Data Scientist is a senior, hands-on individual contributor on our Engineering, Data Platform team. This is a full-time, remote role open to candidates based in the United States or Canada, with no direct reports.

 

StoreForce helps specialty retailers run their stores, from workforce scheduling to performance analytics, across tens of thousands of locations worldwide. We are building a data platform on Azure Databricks that brings years of sales, traffic, labor, and store execution data from every customer into one governed lakehouse.

 

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will turn that data into forecasts, benchmarks, and recommendations that appear inside our products. This is a full-stack role: you will write the Spark and SQL transformations that shape raw data into trusted tables and features, build and validate the models, and run them in production. You will work in a small platform team with product, engineering, and customer-facing colleagues.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Data Transformation & Feature Engineering

- Own the transformation layer: Spark and SQL transformations that turn raw data already in the lakehouse into silver and gold tables.
- Build and maintain the dimensional model shared across both product lines, along with the tests and reconciliation that keep those tables correct.
- Build reusable, point-in-time correct feature tables over the full cross-tenant history.
- Map each customer’s configurable metrics to one governed schema.

2. Semantic Layer & Retail KPIs

- Implement StoreForce’s retail KPI logic in the governed semantic layer (Unity Catalog Metric Views), including fiscal calendars, 53-week comparisons, comp days, and targets.
- Ensure dashboards, applications, models, and AI agents all use the same certified numbers.

3. Forecasting & Insight Products

- Develop, backtest, and ship forecasting models for traffic, sales, and labor demand at store, day, and intraday grain.
- Start from simple baselines and add complexity only where accuracy improves.
- Deliver the wider set of insight products: store clustering, anomaly detection, and conversion and labor driver analysis.
- Build cross-customer benchmarking and analysis that links store execution (tasks, audits, training) to sales results.

4. Production Machine Learning

- Manage experiment tracking and the model registry in MLflow and Unity Catalog.
- Run scheduled batch scoring that writes predictions back to gold tables.
- Monitor models for accuracy, drift, and cost, and retrain when the numbers call for it.

5. Customer Data Protection & AI Analytics

- Protect customer data in everything you build: models and benchmarks that train across customers expose aggregate signal only.
- Ensure every output respects per-tenant row and column security.
- Improve the natural-language analytics experience (Databricks Genie and LLM-based agents) by curating the semantic layer, building evaluation sets, and measuring answer quality.

6. Collaboration & Communication

- Frame problems with product and customer teams.
- Design tests that measure whether a model changed an outcome.
- Explain results and limits to non-technical audiences.

Other duties as assigned by your manager and senior leadership.

 

QUALIFICATIONS  
Competencies Required:

- Analytical Rigor - Applies sound statistics and says clearly when the data cannot support a conclusion
- Full-Stack Ownership - Owns the work end to end, from raw data and transformations to models running in production
- Pragmatism - Starts with simple baselines and adds complexity only where it improves results
- Customer & Product Focus - Frames problems around product and customer outcomes and measures real impact
- Data Stewardship - Protects customer data and treats data correctness as non-negotiable
- Communication - Explains results and limits clearly to engineers, product managers, and non-technical audiences

EXPERIENCE / KNOWLEDGE

- 5+ years in data science or machine learning, with models you built running in production and used by a product or by customers
- Strong Python for data and modeling work (pandas or Polars, scikit-learn, gradient boosting such as LightGBM or XGBoost) and strong SQL (window functions, complex joins, query optimization)
- Depth in time series forecasting: seasonality, holidays and calendar effects, backtesting, and choosing error metrics that match the business decision
- Hands-on transformation work: you have built and maintained the tested, version-controlled tables your models train on, in SQL and Spark or a similar engine (dbt, Snowflake, BigQuery)
- Production machine learning practice: experiment tracking, a model registry, scheduled scoring, monitoring, and retraining, using MLflow or an equivalent
- Sound statistics: experimental design, uncertainty, and the judgment to say when the data cannot support a conclusion
- Clear written and spoken communication with engineers, product managers, and customers.

If you meet most of these qualifications and are strong in forecasting and SQL, we encourage you to apply.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Production experience on Databricks:  
  Unity Catalog, Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines and Lakeflow Jobs, MLflow, Feature Store, Model Serving, and Metric Views
- Experience with hierarchical and intermittent forecasting, and with dimensional modeling, incremental processing, and CI/CD for data transformations
- Experience in retail, workforce management, labor scheduling, or store operations analytics
- Experience with multi-tenant SaaS data, including modeling across customers while keeping each customer’s data isolated
- Experience with optimization methods (for example, labor coverage or schedule optimization) or causal inference
- Experience building with LLM providers (Anthropic Claude and OpenAI) and evaluating LLM applications over structured data: Genie, agent frameworks, evaluation sets, and guardrails
- A graduate degree in statistics, computer science, operations research, or another quantitative field, or equivalent experience.

TECHNICAL ENVIRONMENTYou don’t need experience with every technology named here.

- Platform - Azure Databricks; the platform team brings data from our multi-tenant SQL Server estate into the lakehouse, and your work starts there
- Transformation - PySpark, Spark SQL, and Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
- Storage - Delta Lake on Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
- Governance - Unity Catalog for governance, features, models, and Metric Views
- Training & Scoring - MLflow and Lakeflow Jobs for training and batch scoring; Model Serving where a real-time endpoint is needed
- Serving - Databricks SQL and Lakebase for serving results
- AI Analytics - Genie with Claude or OpenAI models for natural-language analytics
- Delivery - Everything as code through Declarative Automation Bundles and CI/CD

 

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS (KPIs)

- Forecast accuracy for traffic, sales, and labor demand models against baselines and agreed targets, in backtesting and in production
- Reconciliation of governed KPIs to the existing application’s numbers, and test pass rates on silver and gold tables
- Number of models and insight products shipped into production and adopted by customers
- Measured impact of models on customer outcomes, validated through designed tests
- Model health in production: scoring job success, drift detection, retraining cadence, and compute cost
- Zero cross-tenant data exposure across models, benchmarks, and outputs
- Natural-language analytics answer quality measured against evaluation sets
- Satisfaction of product, engineering, and customer-facing teams with the clarity and usefulness of analyses.
